evals.prompt: I teach first-year cell biology. Can you make me one interactive figure that shows how ATP synthase makes ATP in mitochondria, the polished kind, as a single HTML file I can open in class? White background. I want students to see the protons turning the rotor and the ATP coming out.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page with one framed isometric figure of a mammalian ATP synthase standing through a patch of inner mitochondrial membrane, on a crafted mount with a scale bar in nm. The membrane is a bilayer slab about 4–5 nm thick with head-group dots and section faces, split or cut around the protein so nothing is sunk in. The c-ring has 8 subunits (bovine), F1 is three α and three β subunits alternating, faces the matrix, and γ turns inside it; protons enter from the intermembrane space through the a-subunit and leave into the matrix. The model is a pure module with named constants and a SOURCES list: 8 H+ per turn, 3 ATP per turn, 120° steps with dwells (substeps optional), and the readout shows protons, angle and ATP made with the real rate and the playback scale. Numbered legend keys name the c-ring, a-subunit, γ stalk, α3β3 head, peripheral stalk and membrane and light their parts on hover; there are no floating labels. Curved bodies are smooth-shaded from analytic profiles, shapes are recorded with kit/audit.mjs and `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`, the line check prints 0, and the biology review (counts, direction, compartments, scale, sources) is written out alongside 4x close-ups of the protein–membrane contact and the subunit seams.

evals.prompt: For a microbiology explainer on chemotaxis, make an interactive isometric figure of E. coli swimming: show the flagellar motor in the cell envelope and how switching rotation direction makes it run or tumble. React component for our Next.js site plus a static HTML preview I can look at now. Dark theme.
evals.expected_output: A React TSX component (geometry in plain .ts modules, static art in a server component, one 'use client' live component) and a standalone dark HTML preview. The figure opens a Gram-negative E. coli envelope (outer membrane, thin peptidoglycan in the periplasm, inner membrane) at a flagellar motor built from rings on one axis, with stator units around the rotor and the hook leading to a helical filament drawn with kit/tube.mjs, its helix laid across the screen so no bend pinches. The cell body is a capsule from an analytic lathe profile at true proportions (about 2 µm by 1 µm) with a scale bar. Counter-clockwise rotation bundles the filaments into a run and clockwise unbundles them into a tumble; the model holds the direction as a signed value with true run and tumble durations (about 1 s and 0.1 s), and the readout shows direction, rotation rate with its playback scale, and swimming state. Legend keys name the motor parts. Painter's order is correct where the filament crosses the cell, the audit passes with zero problems and 4x close-ups of the envelope layers and motor rings were taken and read.

evals.prompt: make an isometric svg of a leaf cross-section showing how stomata open and close, for a botany lecture slide. light theme, lots of fine detail, just give me the svg file and a png preview
evals.expected_output: A standalone light SVG file (styles embedded) of a block cut from a eudicot leaf, its section faces showing in order the cuticle, upper epidermis, palisade mesophyll as upright column cells, spongy mesophyll with real air spaces, a vein with xylem toward the upper side and phloem toward the lower inside a bundle sheath, and the lower epidermis with kidney-shaped guard-cell pairs around stomatal pores. Cells are solids with cell walls as even gaps, section faces use their own darker token set with no hatching, and chloroplast green, if used, is a token confined to cells that contain chloroplasts. A scale bar in µm sits on the mount. Monochrome apart from that, no floating labels, every texture ends on an edge or fades, no line passes through a part. A PNG preview and 4x close-ups of the guard cells and the vein were made and looked at, and the counts and layer order were checked against the biology review.

evals.prompt: For a molecular biology course page, make an interactive figure of a bacterial ribosome translating an mRNA. I want to see the tRNAs moving through the A, P and E sites and the protein chain growing. One HTML file, dark theme, it should hold up when students zoom in.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone dark HTML page of a bacterial 70S ribosome (50S and 30S subunits as distinct turned or assembled bodies, about 20–25 nm across, with a scale bar) on a model stand, with an mRNA strand drawn as a tube with a cross-section running through the small subunit and read 5' to 3'. tRNAs enter the A site, shift to P and leave from E, one codon per step, and the polypeptide grows N to C out of the exit tunnel in the large subunit. The model holds the mRNA sequence, the genetic code for its codons and a true elongation rate (about 10–20 amino acids per second in bacteria), and the readout names the codon, amino acid, chain length and rate with its playback scale. Motion steps and dwells instead of sliding uniformly. Legend keys name the subunits, sites, mRNA, tRNA and chain. Tubes are recorded and the audit passes, crossings are in true depth order, and the biology review (polarity, site order, scale) is written out with 4x close-ups of the tRNA–mRNA contact.

evals.prompt: For a zoology article on how fish breathe, make an interactive isometric figure of a bony fish gill arch showing countercurrent exchange: water flowing one way over the lamellae and blood flowing the other way. Light theme, standalone HTML, fine detail.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page of one gill arch from a bony fish, cut to show its two rows of gill filaments and the thin lamellae on each filament, with afferent and efferent vessels drawn as tubes from kit/tube.mjs and the gill rakers on the inner edge of the arch, on a mount with a mm-scale bar and a label plate naming the species. Water flow and blood flow run in opposite directions, and the model computes the oxygen gradient along a lamella so the readout shows water and blood O2 at points along it and the overall extraction, with a toggle or slider to compare against concurrent flow. Any flow tint is a token with light and dark values that the no-WebGL fallback matches. Legend keys name the arch, filaments, lamellae, vessels and rakers. Vessels leave their ports on the normal, are gapped where anything wraps them and never pass through the arch; the audit passes with zero problems and 4x close-ups of the vessel junctions and lamellae were read in both themes.

evals.prompt: For a lab methods tutorial, make an interactive figure of an agarose gel electrophoresis tank with a DNA ladder and three samples running. Show the bands separating by size when the power is on. One HTML file, light theme.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page of a horizontal gel tank as a real instrument: a buffer tank with a lid, platinum electrodes with the black cathode at the well end and the red anode at the far end, a gel tray with a comb's wells, a power supply with a display drawn in the plane of its face and its leads routed as cables that land on real terminals. DNA runs toward the anode, and band positions come from a model where migration falls with the logarithm of fragment length, with a ladder of named sizes and three samples whose fragment sizes are constants; the readout shows voltage, field strength in V/cm, run time and the size of the band under the pointer. Bands are drawn in the gel's plane and clipped to their lanes, and any stain colour is a token. Legend keys name the tank parts. Cables pass through nothing and the audit and line check pass; 4x close-ups of the wells, bands and electrode terminals were read.
